messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager - cross-region routing anomaly detected
incident-bot: 09:12 UTC - spike in 5xx and increased p95 latency for requests routed from eu-west2 -> us-east1. Autoscaler/weight controller observed oscillating route weights. Likely cause: rapid weight adjustments + short DNS TTLs. Impact: ~12-18% increased error rate for affected customers.

alice (oncall): I'm paged, looking now. @bob can you confirm if any config rollouts happened in the last 15m?

bob (netops): checking controller logs... yeah I see an operator job at 09:07 that adjusted weights for eu-west2->us-east1 to shift 30%->60% for blue variant, then controller auto-rebalanced back around 09:10. TTL for our regional steer DNS is 30s. That explains oscillation.

carol (sre): stacking: short TTL + controller feedback loop => oscillation -> packet loss + retries -> cascading latency. Oncall runbook: 1) pause auto-weighting, 2) apply temporary pinned weight, 3) raise TTL to 300s, 4) monitor.

alice (oncall): doing step 1 now. Pausing weight controller (rbac job).

bob (netops): paused autopilot at 09:16 UTC (`kubectl annotate cm/route-controller autopilot=disabled --overwrite`). See snippet:
```
kubectl get events -n routing | tail -n 20
09:07 operator job: apply weights {eu-west2:60}
09:09 controller: observed increased latency, rebalanced {eu-west2:28}
09:11 controller: backoff -> reapply weights
```

carol (sre): applying pinned weight for eu-west2 -> us-east1 to 40% stable at 09:18. Increasing DNS TTL to 300s (route-dns zone).

erin (eng-plat): pushed DNS TTL change via infra pipeline (change-id: infra-4321). Propagating now. I also added a short-lived routing rule to prefer local-region endpoints for high latency traces.

dave (support): customers reporting higher error rates: ticket #C-9872 (SaaS onboarding) and #C-9884 (payment microservice). Informing them we're mitigating, ETA ~20m.

alice (oncall): escalation to engineering lead: @erin assigned. Notifying status page team to post: "Partial degraded performance for some cross-region requests; mitigation in progress."

bob (netops): ran active probes to endpoints and traceroutes. Example probe log:
```
> probe eu-west2->api.example.com
09:14: SYN timeout -> retried
09:17: path shows 3% packet loss via transit-b
09:19: no errors after pin applied
```

carol (sre): metrics look better: 5xx rate down from 15% to 2% after pin + TTL change. p95 latency trending down. Keeping monitoring on until stable for 30m.

dave (support): updated customer tickets with notes and timeline. Customers acknowledged, one asked for postmortem.

erin (eng-plat): rolling a small config change to prevent weight controller from reacting to <1m spikes (throttle window=120s). Change-id infra-4327 -> will deploy after 10m smoke.

alice (oncall): handing off to @carol for postmitigation & RCA follow-up. I'm signing out for the hour. Handoff notes: paused controller, pinned-weight=40%, TTL=300s, probes green.

carol (sre): taking over. I'll own the incident until RCA posted. Preliminary cause: controller autoscaling + operator job + very short DNS TTLs creating feedback loop. Next steps: RCA, permanent fix to controller hysteresis, add guardrails on operator rollouts, increase default steer TTL to 60s.

bob (netops): we should also add an operator job preflight check to avoid conflicting immediate rollouts. Filing infra task INF-2123.

dave (support): status page updated to resolved for customer-notice at 09:34 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident resolved at 09:34 UTC - mitigation effective, monitoring window started.

carol (sre): resolution summary posted to #postmortems; owner assigned: carol. ETA for full postmortem: 48h.

alice (oncall): :thumbsup: good job team.

erin (eng-plat): follow-up action items created: [optimize-controller-hysteresis, add-rollout-preflight, default-ttl-bump]. Linking infra changes to this incident.

bob (netops): will run a canary of the throttle change in staging tomorrow 08:00 UTC.

carol (sre): closing thread here, will add timeline + logs to the postmortem doc. If anyone has additional data, DM me. :memo:
